LESSON: SINGING GAMES

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Singing Games

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Singing Games. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. apply the aspects of singing games with game aspects, singing, movement, props and costumes in performing singing games to enhance the skills of performance,
2. take precautions during performance of singing games for own and others safety,
3. practice game etiquette for own and others respect, e) share available resources during performance of singing games for equity and integrity, f) appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. apply the aspects of singing games with game aspects, singing, movement, props and costumes in performing singing games to enhance the skills of performance,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to apply the aspects of singing games with game aspects, singing, movement, props and costumes in performing singing games to enhance the skills of performance,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. take precautions during performance of singing games for own and others safety,
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to take precautions during performance of singing games for own and others safety,. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

3. practice game etiquette for own and others respect, e) share available resources during performance of singing games for equity and integrity, f) appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE

Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At home, obey your parent when they ask you to wash your plate. That shows obedience.

Example 2: Tell the truth if you break a cup. Saying what really happened is honesty.

Example 3: Thank God for your family before you sleep. A short prayer can be: “Thank you God for today.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Singing Games.
2. Explain Singing Games to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Singing Games.
4. Show that you can: apply the aspects of singing games with game aspects, singing, movement, props and costumes in performing singing games to enhance the skills of performance,
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Singing Games. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Singing Games important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. apply the aspects of singing games with game aspects, singing, movement, props and costumes in performing singing games to enhance the skills of performance,
2. take precautions during performance of singing games for own and others safety,
3. practice game etiquette for own and others respect, e) share available resources during performance of singing games for equity and integrity, f) appreciate and enjoy performing singing games from the local cultures. 307 NOT FOR SALE

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
